key_insight: ActCam enables zero-shot joint control of an actor's 3D motion and per-frame camera parameters in generated videos by leveraging pretrained image-to-video diffusion models conditioned on scene depth and motion signals. It transfers a driving performance into a new scene while allowing intrinsic and extrinsic camera control without task-specific retraining.
problem_solved: Provides fine-grained, joint control over both actor performance (3D motion) and cinematography (camera trajectory and settings) in video generation, eliminating the need for supervised retraining or separate camera/motion pipelines.
method: Zero-shot motion transfer: extract motion from a driving video and condition the generation model to reproduce the actor's 3D performance in a target scene.
Per-frame camera conditioning: encode intrinsic (focal length, aperture-like effects) and extrinsic (pose, trajectory) parameters per frame to steer cinematography during synthesis.
Depth-aware diffusion backbone: build on pretrained image-to-video diffusion models that accept scene depth (and motion/pose) conditioning to ensure consistent 3D-aware rendering across frames.
impact: Enables artists and ML practitioners to jointly control performance and camera for controllable, cinematic video synthesis without expensive retraining, accelerating applications in virtual production, VFX, and dataset creation for downstream 3D/vision tasks.

paper_title: ActCam: Zero-Shot Joint Camera and 3D Motion Control for Video Generation
paper_authors: Omar El Khalifi, Thomas Rossi, Oscar Fossey, Thibault Fouque, Ulysse Mizrahi
